Angelic Davis (angelic.davis@enron.com) sent 6 unique messages to dana.davis@enron.com between 2001-10-01 and 2001-11-01. I filtered on sender, recipient (To or Cc) and date range, and the 6 results had 6 distinct ids, so none were duplicates. I only printed the first five, and the ids below are from those.

ANSWER: 6
SOURCES: Eec51ca95dc10, E78c208665714, Ea4671be47808, Ea9e43a0d11aa, Ef703ce92e611

eSource@ENRON (40enron@enron.com) sent the most messages on 2001-09-05. It sent 23 that day, out of 160 for September 2001. The next highest days were 2001-09-28 with 19 and 2001-09-14 with 16. I counted messages by UTC date using the sender address filter. I didn't open any individual messages, so I'm citing none.

ANSWER: 2001-09-05
SOURCES:

Jeff Dasovich sent the most messages to Richard Sanders in that window. I filtered for messages sent to richard.sanders@enron.com (To or Cc) from 2001-05-29 up to but not including 2001-06-05. That gave 37 messages, and Dasovich sent 8 of them. Susan Mara was next with 5, then Janette Elbertson with 4. The sources below are three of Dasovich's messages.

ANSWER: jeff.dasovich@enron.com
SOURCES: Ec64a0fe2fe15, Efbeffae21bed, Eb4461cb03bfd

Vince Kaminski sent the most messages in April 2001 to vkaminski@aol.com. That address appeared in the To or Cc of 173 of his 458 messages that month, counting each message once.

The next highest was his own enron.com address, with 135. If you count only other people, the top recipient is Shirley Crenshaw at shirley.crenshaw@enron.com, with 54. I didn't open any individual messages, so I have no message IDs to cite.

ANSWER: vkaminski@aol.com
SOURCES:

The number 703-227-8777 appears in one message, **Ef817f5aac97c**. Its subject is "FW: 082501 Enron Confirmation", and it was sent on 2001-08-24. The sender is Bryant Frihart (bryant.frihart@enron.com).

The number is written as "703.227.8777 Phone" in the body. The message went to hayhurstb@paceglobal.com, with Tammy Gilmore and C. Giron on Cc.

I searched for the number with several separator styles (dashes, dots, spaces, parentheses). That search returned only this one message.

ANSWER: bryant.frihart@enron.com
SOURCES: Ef817f5aac97c

Vince Kaminski sent the most messages on 2001-04-25, with 47. I counted messages from vince.kaminski@enron.com in April 2001 by UTC date. The next highest days were 2001-04-11 with 37 and 2001-04-27 with 36. I didn't open any individual messages, so the source list is empty.

ANSWER: 2001-04-25
SOURCES:

The reference EB-2934 appears in one message, E2093dccd9417. Robin Barbe sent it on 2000-12-05, with the subject "PSEG Meeting". It went to Chris Germany and Dick Jenkins. The matching line reads "50,000/d @ Transco Zone 6, on Tuesday, December 5, 3:00 p.m., in EB-2934." In that line, EB-2934 looks like a meeting room.

ANSWER: robin.barbe@enron.com
SOURCES: E2093dccd9417

The reference ORE-7509 appears in exactly one message, **E2083b9620d07**. It was sent on 2002-02-27 with the subject "(CMS-26) NOTICE OF INTENTION TO TRANSFER MEMBERSHIP".

The sender is marketing@nymex.com, shown as "Exchange Information @ENRON". The message sits in the deleted_items folder of custodian shackleton-s. The matching line reads "Edward Orenchuk (ORE-7509)", so the reference is attached to a person's name in a NYMEX membership transfer notice.

ANSWER: marketing@nymex.com
SOURCES: E2083b9620d07

Across the 29 messages in that window that contain "Raptor", 14 distinct sender addresses sent at least one.

I used a case-insensitive grep over the full text of every message, headers included, for 2001-11-01 up to but not including 2001-12-01. It returned all 29 matching messages, so no hits were cut off by the limit. I then lowercased the sender addresses and counted the unique ones.

ANSWER: 14
SOURCES:

The sender who sent the most matching messages was enron.announcements@enron.com, with 7 of the 35 messages in the window that contain "Azurix". I ran a case-insensitive grep over the full text of every message from 2000-12-01 up to but not including 2001-01-01. The grep returned all 35 matches, so nothing was cut off by the result limit. Next was jeffrey.shankman@enron.com with 5.

I didn't read any of the messages, so I'm giving only two ids from the hits as sources. I didn't check that these two are among the 7 from the top sender.

ANSWER: enron.announcements@enron.com
SOURCES: Ed90dc526aef5, Ecfc8c3a0f4d8

More messages containing "Dynegy" were sent on 2000-05-23 than on any other date in May 2000. A case-insensitive grep over the full text of every message, headers included, matched 103 messages in that window. 14 of them are dated 2000-05-23. The next highest were 10 each on 2000-05-04 and 2000-05-19.

I counted by the date field on each matching message and didn't open any messages, so I have no message ids to cite.

ANSWER: 2000-05-23
SOURCES:

The only message that mentions 703-227-8777 is Ef817f5aac97c. It was sent on 2001-08-24 by bryant.frihart@enron.com, and the number appears there as "703.227.8777". That sender sent 2 messages in August 2001 (UTC), counting from 2001-08-01 up to but not including 2001-09-01.

ANSWER: 2
SOURCES: Ef817f5aac97c
